transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-10 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Aaron Patel, Diego Morales (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Samir Gupta, Marta Ruiz, Oliver Lee (Verdigris)
---
00:00 Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the CSM, really excited to kick off the Verdigris onboarding. Quick agenda: tenant mapping, security checklist, staging connectivity, and pilot timeline. Anything to add?
00:18 Lena Ortiz: That sounds good. I want to make sure we cover multi-tenant isolation — we run separate models per team and need clear boundaries.
00:26 Maya Chen: Yep, noted. Aaron, Diego you want to start on tenant mapping?
00:33 Aaron Patel: Yeah, sure. So our usual pattern is workspaces at the org level, then "environments" for staging/prod. For Verdigris we recommend a two-workspace mapping — one for "platform" teams and one for "product" teams, then envs under each. That way RBAC is straightforward.
00:52 Samir Gupta: Quick question — can we map a single workspace to multiple VPCs? We have segmented networks per team.
00:58 Aaron Patel: Short answer: you can have multiple subnets talk to a single workspace via peering, but we usually recommend separate workspaces if you want hard isolation and separate billing. Otherwise you get logical isolation only.
01:15 Marta Ruiz: So billing separation is a big one for us, yes. We want cost per product line visible.
01:21 Maya Chen: Understood — for the pilot we can scope two distinct workspaces to keep cost and telemetry separated. We'll include cost reporting in the pilot metrics.
01:34 Oliver Lee: On the security front, are we looking at Redwood hosted or private deployment? Our legal prefers private deployment inside our VPC, but engineering prefers Redwood hosted to iterate faster.
01:48 Diego Morales: If you choose private, we do a private control plane install or on-prem agent depending on the option. It buys you full network isolation and KMS integration. Hosted is faster to get started; we can still offer VPC peering + egress IPs for allow-listing.
02:02 Samir Gupta: For the pilot can we do hosted plus VPC peering? That would let us test quickly, then move to private if everything looks good.
02:09 Maya Chen: That's our typical path. We'll provision a hosted staging workspace with static egress IPs you can whitelist. Aaron will set that up.
02:20 Aaron Patel: I'll need CIDR ranges and the team that owns the firewall rules. Samir, can you confirm who's the network contact?
02:26 Samir Gupta: Yeah, that's me and I can make firewall changes but I need the concrete IP list.
02:30 Aaron Patel: Great, Samir I'll provide the IPs. I might mis-say some things in the call but it's a small list, I'll email it.
02:40 Lena Ortiz: Also curious about KV cache. We have long-running sessions and caching behavior matters for latency. How do you manage per-tenant KV caches?
02:50 Aaron Patel: We shard the KV cache by workspace and model instance; ephemeral caches for staged requests. Sometimes the transcript system hears "K-V cake" — ignore that. For large sessions we can pin a model instance to a workspace to improve cache locality.
03:08 Marta Ruiz: Good to know, latency is a top metric.
03:12 Maya Chen: We'll capture both p50/p95 and per-request token costs in the pilot dashboard.
03:20 Oliver Lee: On compliance, we need SOC 2 type II evidence, logs retention policy, and KMS integration details. Will that be covered?
03:29 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 report and the security datasheet. For KMS we support customer-managed keys through major cloud KMS providers and can show the encryption flow.
03:40 Oliver Lee: Do you have HSM options or is it only KMS?
03:44 Diego Morales: We integrate with HSM-backed KMS in enterprise plans — it's part of the Private deployment offering.
03:50 Samir Gupta: Any extra latency penalty with customer-managed KMS?
03:54 Aaron Patel: Minimal, most encryption is at rest and the serving path caches decrypted keys for a session. We can share numbers from comparable customers.
04:05 Maya Chen: Next up network: staging connectivity details and the peering plan. Aaron?
04:12 Aaron Patel: For hosted staging we provide a small set of static egress IPs and an optional proxy connector to push logs. If you want VPC peering we can do that too but it requires a bit more firewall and route config. Either way we'll need CIDR and bastion details if you're behind strict NAT.
04:31 Samir Gupta: We'll share CIDR ranges. For peering we prefer AWS Transit Gateway. Is that supported?
04:37 Diego Morales: We can peer into TGW for enterprise Private installs; for hosted workspaces we usually use NAT/egress IPs — TGW peering is supported on Dedicated/Private customers.
04:49 Lena Ortiz: Timeline: how long from documentation handoff to a working pilot?
04:53 Maya Chen: Typical start is 1-2 weeks for staging with hosted and 4-8 weeks for private deployments. Given your preference for hosted->private, pilot could start in ~10 business days if we get artifacts quickly.
05:08 Marta Ruiz: That aligns with our internal quarter planning. Success criteria for the pilot: stable latency under 300ms p95 for inference, integration with our SSO, and stable cost-per-1000-token estimate.
05:22 Maya Chen: Good clear metrics — we'll put those into the pilot template.
05:26 Oliver Lee: About SSO — we use SAML with Okta. Requirements?
05:30 Aaron Patel: We support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning and can map groups into workspace roles. We'll need metadata from Okta, and the person who owns the SSO config.
05:39 Marta Ruiz: That's me and I'll pair with Oliver.
05:42 Maya Chen: Great. On audit logs, you want per-user action logs retained for at least 12 months?
05:49 Oliver Lee: Prefer 24 but 12 minimum. Also we want immutable logs if possible.
05:53 Diego Morales: We can export logs to your S3 bucket or SIEM and retain 24 months on our enterprise package. Immutable retention is supported via object lock on S3, we'd coordinate ACLs.
06:08 Samir Gupta: Will we get request-level traces for debugging?
06:11 Aaron Patel: Yes, we provide request_id traces, token-level timing, and per-call headers. We sanitize PII by default but can toggle retention policies per workspace.
06:24 Marta Ruiz: Any blockers on profiling model outputs for quality monitoring? We want evals hooks.
06:29 Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize offers evals tied to prompt sets; during the pilot you can upload canonical prompts and we'll run regression checks. We'll show the evaluation UI in the pilot demo.
06:41 Lena Ortiz: Excellent. For billing and quotas — if we spin up two workspaces, can we have separate billing centers?
06:47 Diego Morales: We'll link usage to billing tags per workspace; you can export usage to your billing system. For charges, there's per-token accounting and reserved capacity options later.
06:58 Samir Gupta: On reserved capacity later — do you support committed bursts? We don't want sudden throttles during peak batch jobs.
07:04 Aaron Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity and predictable throughput; we'll surface autoscale policies in the console. For pilot we stick to hosted with soft limits.
07:14 Marta Ruiz: Okay, one more security nit: network egress logging and who owns the keys to logs?
07:19 Oliver Lee: We want logs encrypted with our KMS and S3 bucket ownership in our account.
07:23 Diego Morales: That's supported for Private; for hosted we can push logs to your S3 and encrypt with your KMS key but the object ownership model changes slightly. We'll provide exact configuration steps.
07:36 Maya Chen: Alright, let's run through the artifacts we need from Verdigris to get started. Samir?
07:42 Samir Gupta: I'll send CIDR ranges, the person who manages firewall rules, and Okta metadata. Also we need a service account for API access to test.
07:51 Maya Chen: Noted. Oliver, you'll send the security contact and any compliance constraints?
07:55 Oliver Lee: Yes, I'll fill out the security questionnaire.
07:58 Marta Ruiz: I'll provide the pilot success criteria doc and who the stakeholders for signoff are.
08:04 Maya Chen: Great. Quick pause — any concerns about inference cost predictability during pilot?
08:10 Lena Ortiz: We worry about token spikes from exploratory prompts in prod. How do we guard?
08:16 Aaron Patel: You can set per-route soft caps and alerts. We also provide sampling of high-cost requests and token trimming suggestions via Optimize.
08:27 Marta Ruiz: Will Redwood's SDKs enforce max tokens automatically?
08:30 Aaron Patel: SDKs can include defaults and wrappers; we can provide example middleware to enforce max tokens and pre-flight checks.
08:39 Maya Chen: Okay, timeline recap — Maya to send runbook by end of this week, Aaron to stand up staging and send IPs, Verdigris to fill questionnaire and send network details.
08:50 Samir Gupta: One more item: do you support model pinning by tag? We need to pin a specific quantized model for consistency.
08:56 Aaron Patel: Yes, model pinning is supported and rollouts are controlled per workspace. We'll include the model versioning plan in the pilot template.
09:06 Lena Ortiz: Are there any known gotchas for large context lengths with your runtime? We push 32k contexts sometimes.
09:12 Diego Morales: We support high context models but performance varies by kernel and quantization. For 32k contexts we recommend certain model families — we'll include a compatibility matrix. Occasionally the auto-transcribe reads "thirty-two Kay" as "thirty-two K" which is fine.
09:30 Marta Ruiz: Great. Let's shift to scheduling the pilot demo — week of Oct 18 works for us.
09:36 Maya Chen: I'll send a Doodle after the call.
09:39 Aaron Patel: I'll prepare a short checklist for infra that includes egress IPs, Okta metadata, test API key, and sample prompts.
09:47 Oliver Lee: On legal, we'll likely need SCCs for data transfer to US regions. Any immediate blockers?
09:52 Maya Chen: We have standard SCCs and can route to EU regions if required. We'll flag any special data residency requests to the account team.
09:59 Samir Gupta: Great. Anything else?
10:02 Lena Ortiz: One small thing: can we limit debug traces in prod to a sampled percentage?
10:07 Aaron Patel: Yes, sampling and redaction rules are configurable per workspace.
10:12 Marta Ruiz: Perfect.
10:15 Maya Chen: OK, let's do a recap of action items — I'll read them out and then we'll close.
10:20 Maya Chen: (recap) Maya to send runbook and pilot template by 2027-10-13; Aaron to provide staging IPs and create staging routes by 2027-10-14; Samir to provide CIDRs and firewall contact by 2027-10-12; Oliver to complete security questionnaire by 2027-10-17. Verdigris to confirm pilot stakeholder signoff and schedule demo week of 2027-10-18.
10:41 Marta Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
10:43 Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and invite. Bye.
